subject: computer-science

items.q: What is the difference between serial and parallel transmission?
items.correct: Serial sends one bit at a time down a single wire; parallel sends several bits at once down multiple wires.
items.misconception: Serial and parallel transmission send data in exactly the same way.
items.why: Serial uses one channel bit-by-bit; parallel uses several channels simultaneously.

items.q: Why is serial transmission preferred over long distances?
items.correct: Parallel wires suffer from skew and interference over distance, so serial is more reliable.
items.misconception: Parallel is used over long distances because it is faster.
items.why: Over distance, parallel bits arrive out of step (skew), so serial (e.g. USB) is used instead.

items.correct: Data can travel in both directions, but only one direction at a time.
items.misconception: Half-duplex means data travels in both directions at the same time.
items.why: Both-directions-at-once is full-duplex; half-duplex takes turns, like a walkie-talkie.

items.q: What is a data packet made up of?
items.correct: A header, the payload (the actual data), and a trailer.
items.misconception: A data packet is just the raw data with nothing added.
items.why: Headers and trailers carry addressing and error-checking information needed for delivery.

items.q: What does a parity check do?
items.correct: It detects whether a single bit has changed during transmission, using a parity bit.
items.misconception: A parity check automatically corrects any errors in the data.
items.why: Parity only detects errors (and not even all of them) — it cannot correct them.

items.q: What is the purpose of a checksum?
items.correct: A value calculated from the data and recalculated at the destination to detect transmission errors.
items.misconception: A checksum encrypts the data so it cannot be read.
items.why: Checksums verify integrity, not confidentiality — encryption is a separate process.

items.q: Does a check digit correct mistakes in a number?
items.correct: No — it only detects errors in entered numbers like a barcode or ISBN.
items.misconception: A check digit fixes any mistakes in the number automatically.
items.why: It flags that an error exists; the number must be re-entered or rechecked.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science (0478) syllabus; Data Transmission
